about: The instrument library's recipes (scripts/instrument-packs.js, `just instrument-packs`; docs/design/music.md rung 6). libraries: the raw CC0 downloads under E:\HumanityOS\instruments-src, with the size and SHA-256 recorded when they were downloaded (docs/reference/instrument-sources.md); a changed file is refused. packs: the core set (ships in the app, data/music) and each downloadable pack (one archive, a GitHub release asset). instruments: which samples each instrument keeps (velocity layers, round robins, a key spread), its part of the score (data/music/parts.ron) and its rank (higher wins when several play one part). Add an instrument by adding a recipe; add a library only after its licence is cleared and its download recorded.

instruments.tuning_note: not measured: a tubular bell's strike note is heard from its upper partials, which the pitch measure cannot follow (it scattered by more than 30 cents on half the bells); VCSL measures within a few cents of 440 on its harmonic instruments

where the measure disagrees with a file name (an octave out when it locks onto a partial, a neighbouring note ringing along, or the hardest hits up to about 50 cents sharp, the way a struck pan sounds) the key follows the MIDI number in the file name, which the hits measured in tune confirm

not measured: a plucked double bass's low, fast-dying notes defeat the pitch measure (it locked onto 10 to 25 Hz or an octave off on 5 of 14 notes and pulled the median 30 cents flat); the library's other instruments measure within 5 cents of A = 440 (trumpet +4.6, trombone +0.7, clarinet +3.7), and its file names are an octave under the sounding pitch

not measured: a tubular bell's strike note is heard from its upper partials, which the pitch measure cannot follow (it scattered by more than 30 cents on half the bells); VCSL measures within a few cents of 440 on its harmonic instruments

where the measure disagrees with a file name (an octave out when it locks onto a partial, a neighbouring note ringing along, or the hardest hits up to about 50 cents sharp, the way a struck pan sounds) the key follows the MIDI number in the file name, which the hits measured in tune confirm
where the measure disagrees with a file name (an octave out when it locks onto a partial) the key follows the note in the file name; every note plays only its own key, as the bank asks
keys from each hit's measured pitch
